chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Isma'il from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman who died and left behind her husband, with no other heir for her. He said: 'If there is no one else, then he has the wealth, and the wife has one-quarter, and whatever remains belongs to the Imam.'
And this report does not contradict what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a husband when his wife dies and he is the only heir?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the husband inherits the entire estate as the sole heir, with the 'one-quarter' reference serving as the baseline marital share that is subsumed by the exclusivity of his inheritance. The remainder is allocated to the Imam (al-Imam), reflecting the Shia doctrine of the Imam's right to inherit from those with no other living relatives, a key distinction from Sunni jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the Imam's role as the general heir (al-'Asabah) in the absence of closer kin.
